einstellungen.text: Twelve eighteen. Your bus driver once left someone behind at Millbrook Lane.
The word stop slowly runs down the glass. You walk up front, to Henrik.
He talks quietly, without taking his eyes off the road.
“I've seen this once before. Just once.”
November eighth, nineteen ninety-eight. The last night before they flooded the valley.
It's pouring rain. Henrik is young and tired. He wants to clock out early.
At Millbrook Lane, a boy is standing in the shelter. With a red schoolbag. He waves.
Henrik drives past. He thinks: he'll catch the next bus.
There was no next bus. By morning the village was empty. Then the water came.
You ask what happened to the boy. Henrik doesn't answer.
You check your phone. Twelve nineteen. November eighth.
It's the exact same night. Twenty-eight years later.
In the window, the three figures sit perfectly still. Like they're waiting.
The lights flicker. The bus turns, even though Henrik holds the wheel straight.
The road gets narrow. Water on the left. Water on the right.
The sign flips again. Last stop: The Dam. This route doesn't even go there.
